numbering: Base fronts carry two digits. The first digit says which family the front belongs to: 2 is an Under front, 5 is an Over front, 4 is an Even front, 3 is an odd 3-4 front. The second digit says where the backers sit: 9 keeps all three backers in the box, 5 puts the Sam on the line, 7 puts the Will on the line, 3 puts both the Sam and the Will on the line. A safety in the box gets a word: Sup means the strong safety is down, Fup means the free safety is down. Sub fronts use a different pair of digits: the first is how many down linemen are on the field and the second is how many backers. 42 is four linemen and two backers (nickel), 41 is four and one (dime), 33 is three and three (nickel with an odd line), 32 is three and two (dime with an odd line). A word after the digits sets the shape: nothing means an even line, Under means an Under shape, Over means an Over shape. Jam means the center and both guards each have a lineman on them. Bear is a Jam with a Choke defender added on the tight end.
techniques: Line spots are numbered from the center outward on each side. 0 is nose to nose on the center. Shade (a 1 technique) is the nose moved to one shoulder of the center, which makes him an A gap player. 2i is the inside shoulder of the guard, 2 is head up on the guard, 3 is the outside shoulder of the guard. 4i is the inside shoulder of the tackle, 4 is head up on the tackle, 5 is the outside shoulder of the tackle. 6i is the inside shoulder of the tight end, 6 is head up on the tight end, 9 is outside the tight end. An i after a number always means the inside shoulder of that blocker.

players.means: Sam. The strong side outside backer, lined up to the tight end side.
Mike. In an odd front he is the strong side inside backer; in a 4-3 he is the middle backer.
Jack. The weak side inside backer in an odd front, or in a sub front with three down linemen.
Will. The weak side outside backer, lined up to the open (no tight end) side.
Nose. The middle lineman in an odd front.
Tackle. An interior lineman in a 4-3 front.
End. A defensive end in either an odd front or a 4-3.
Strong safety. Sets to the tight end side.
Free safety. Sets away from the tight end.
Nickel Will. A defensive back who comes in and takes the Will spot.
Nickel Sam. A defensive back who comes in and takes the Sam spot.

alignments.means: The Will sits on the hip of the defensive end on his side, just off the line.
The Sam sits on the hip of the defensive end on his side, just off the line.
The Will walks out of the box to a slot receiver.
The Sam walks out of the box to a slot receiver.
Not defined in the text. In the 45 Wide and 55 Wide pictures the end and the Sam sit next to each other outside the tight end, so it reads as a widened edge. Exact spot unclear.
A defender lines up on the tight end with the end or a backer outside him. The page also states it the other way around: the end covers the tight end and the Sam sits outside.
A backer drops down into the A gap, at the heels of the line.
A backer drops down into the B gap, at the heels of the line.
A backer stands over the center at the heels of the line.
The backers slide toward the weak side.
The backers slide toward the strong side.
The Sam is on the line of scrimmage. In the picture the nickel Will fills his old spot. A backer on the line only gets this tag in sub fronts.

The 3 technique tackle takes an inside move on his own.
A single lineman on an inside move; the number says which technique.

Both ends take an inside move (5 Pinch or 4 Pinch), or both tackles take an inside move (3 Pinch or 2 Pinch), depending on the technique named.
Every lineman takes an inside move, from 5 and 3 technique spots.

coverages.name: Cover 0
coverages.means: Straight man with nobody deep. Both safeties are in the coverage or the rush.
variations: Cover 0 Dog: base personnel, man across with a backer added to the rush for six rushers and no deep defender.
Cover 00 Blitz: nickel personnel, same idea, six rushers and no deep defender.

coverages.name: Cover 1
coverages.means: Man coverage with one safety free in the middle. The other safety is down in the box, on a double, or in the hole.
variations: Cover 1 Wk Dog: free safety down, strong safety free, five rushers (weak side dog).
Cover 1 Hole Wk: free safety down, strong safety free, a hole player underneath, four rushers.
Cover 1 X: free safety doubles X, strong safety free, four rushers.
Cover 1 Dog: strong safety down, free safety free, five rushers.
Cover 1 Rover: free safety down as a lurker (rover), strong safety free, four rushers.
Cover 1 Hole: a backer plugs the hole, free safety free, four rushers.

coverages.name: Cover 11
coverages.means: The nickel version of Cover 1: man with one safety free and the nickel in the coverage.
variations: Cover 11 Rover: strong safety is the lurker, free safety free, four rushers.
Cover 11 (Dog): free safety free, a single dog with the end dropping out, still four rushers.
Cover 11 Blitz: free safety down, strong safety free, five rushers.
Cover 11 Hole: the backers play the back two ways, free safety free, a hole player, four rushers.
Cover 11 Lurk: free safety is the lurker, strong safety free, four rushers.
Cover 11 Dog: strong safety down, free safety free, five rushers.

coverages.name: Cover 2
coverages.means: Two deep halves with five underneath: corners on the flats, backers on the curls and middle, four rushers.
variations: 2 Tampa: three deep and four under, with the Mike running through to the deep middle, the corners sinking to wide halves, hook players reading the quarterback.
Cover 2 Man: two deep halves with man underneath.
Cover 2 Invert Weak: two deep five under, the weak corner and the free safety trade jobs (corner to the half, safety to the flat).
Cover 2 Carry: two deep five under, the flat player carries #2 on a vertical from a landmark drop.
Cover 2C: two deep five under with the corner going over to the slot. The label sits apart from its picture on the page, so the pairing is unclear.

coverages.name: Cover 22
coverages.means: The nickel version of Cover 2: two deep halves, five under, four rushers, with the nickel as a flat or curl player.
variations: Cover 22 Tampa: three deep four under with the Mike running through to the deep middle.
Cover 22 Man: two deep halves with man under.
Cover 22 Invert Weak: corner and free safety trade jobs on the weak side.
Cover 22 Dbl Invert: corner and safety trade jobs on both sides.
Cover 22 Invert: corner and nickel trade jobs on the nickel side.

coverages.name: Cover 3
coverages.means: Three deep thirds and four under (two hooks, two curl-flats) with the strong safety down, four rushers.
variations: Cover 3 Buzz: the Sam and the strong safety trade jobs.
Cover 3 Wk: the free safety is the one who comes down.
Cover 3 Cloud Wk: the weak corner plays the flat (cloud) and the safety behind him takes the third.
Cover 3 Hook: the Will and the free safety trade jobs.
Cover 3 Wk Dog (p44): three deep three under, strong safety down, five rushers.
Cover 3 Blitz (p44): three deep three under, the strong side defensive back rushes, five rushers.
Cover 3 (Wk Dog) (p44): three deep four under, strong safety down, a weak dog with four rushers in all.

coverages.name: Cover 33
coverages.means: The nickel version of Cover 3: three deep, four under, four rushers. The page labels one picture 33 Wk with the strong safety down and the plain 33 with the free safety down weak, so which safety drops may be flipped by the extraction.
variations: Cover 33 Wk: three deep four under; labeled with the strong safety down.
Cover 33 Hook: the Sam and the strong safety trade jobs.
Cover 330 Cloud: dime look, three deep five under, the strong corner plays cloud, only three rushers, a low hole player.
Cover 33 Buzz: the nickel and the free safety trade jobs.
Cover 33 Carry Wk: strong safety down, the nickel takes #2 man on a vertical or out, hook players read the quarterback.

coverages.name: Reno
coverages.means: A bracket coverage: one deep middle player, #2 bracketed on each side with the bracket players passing off crossers, four rushers, with the shell cheated to the passing strength. Drawn against a Dagger concept.
variations: Apex call: take your own #3 to the flat; with no #3, zone off and push #2 over the top.
Wall call: take your own #3 unless he goes to the weak flat, then look for the passing-strength #2 on a shallow, or zone off if there is no back or shallow.
M-M call: straight man on the receiver.

coverages.name: Cover 4
coverages.means: Four deep quarters and three under, four rushers. The outside players carry a zone-match tag on #2 (ZM2).
variations: Cover 44: the nickel version, quarters with flat players on each side.
Cover 44 Trix: quarter, quarter on one side and man on the other, with #3 vertical handled by the quarters side.

Cover 44 Palms: a read coverage. The corner takes #1 vertical unless #2 goes to the flat; the safety takes #2 vertical and expands to #1 if #2 goes flat or under; underneath players wall #2. Plays as four deep three under or two deep five under depending on the read.
Cover 44 Erase: quarter, quarter on one side and man on the other, with the back erased by a man player.

coverages.name: Cover 6
coverages.means: Quarter, quarter to one side and a half to the other: two quarters players with a flat defender on the quarters side, a corner in the flat and a safety over the top on the half side. Hook/curl players underneath, four rushers.
variations: Cover 66: the nickel version of Cover 6.
Cover 66 Invert Wk: the corner and the free safety trade jobs on the half side.
Cover 66 Fist: quarter, quarter with the half side played as 2 Man by the corner, free safety and Will.
Cover 88: the same shell flipped, half to one side and quarter, quarter to the other.

coverages.name: Cover 7
coverages.means: Man bracket coverage with no middle safety: everyone is matched and the safeties are part of the brackets, four rushers. Drawn against 3x1 and 2x2.
variations: Combo: the base call, bracket man with no middle safety.
Combo Doubles: Cone, Bracket, Uber, Cindy, Taxi, Connie. Names only on the page; what each doubles is unclear.

coverages.name: Red zone man
coverages.means: Man coverage calls for the red zone, built from Cover 1 and Cover 0 with hole players and doubles.
variations: Red 11 Hole: man with the free safety doubling, four rushers. Against 3x1 and 2x2. Uses a Train call.
Red 00 Dbl Hole: man with three free players underneath, four rushers. Receivers split as first outside and first inside.
Red 11 Dog: man with a single dog and the free safety doubling.
Red 00 Dog Hole: man with a single dog and two hole players.
Red 000 Dbl Hole: man with three free players and only three rushers.

coverages.name: Stacks and bunch
coverages.means: Rules for man coverage against stacked and bunched receivers. The default is a locked 5-1-3 count, with the Brady box check as the adjustment when man is called.
variations: Box: corner, nickel and strong safety split the bunch by #1 vertical, #2 vertical, first to the flat and first under.
Levels: defenders at different depths, each told to stay alert for rubs and picks.
Lock Triangle: lock plus a combo with help over the top from a two-high shell.
Lock Tango: lock one receiver and tango (first inside, first outside) the other two; off-ball defenders at the same depth pass off receivers.
Top Hat: a gameplan change-up that looks like lock before the snap.
Tango: two defenders split the pair as first inside and first outside.
Triangle: three defenders split the group as first inside, first outside and vertical.
Tophat Tango: shows bump the point or in-and-out before the snap but locks the innermost receiver on a bunch.
Alert Under (p52): a call for the underneath defender.
Zone It (p52): play the group as zone, #1 vertical, #2 vertical, curl/flat. Pack It is the check when man is called.
Bass (p52): a backer and a safety share two receivers as first inside and first outside.
Banjo (p52): two backers share two receivers as first inside and first outside.
Magic (p52): three defenders over two receivers.
